name: permission-rule-engine
what: Permission.evaluate(permission, pattern, ...rulesets) flattens the rulesets and takes the LAST rule whose permission and pattern both wildcard-match the request; with no match it returns {action:'ask', permission, pattern:'*'}. fromConfig turns config entries into rules (a bare string becomes pattern '*', a record maps expanded patterns - ~/, $HOME and ~ expansions - to actions). disabled() hides a tool when the last matching rule is pattern '*' with action deny, mapping edit/write/apply_patch onto the 'edit' permission and the MCP resource tools onto 'read'; visibleTools filters a tool map through it.
invariants: Rule resolution is last-match-wins over a flattened list, so ordering of the merged ruleset is part of the policy.
An unmatched request must default to 'ask', never to 'allow'.
A blanket deny (pattern '*') removes the tool from the model's tool list entirely.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - the absence of a rule is an ask, and a blanket deny removes the capability.
constants: edit-family tools mapped to the 'edit' permission: edit, write, apply_patch (packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts:205)
MCP resource tools mapped to the 'read' permission (packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts:206)

name: permission-ask-queue
what: The permission service keeps a per-instance state of pending requests (Map<ID, {info, Deferred}>) plus an 'approved' rule list accumulated from 'always' replies. ask() evaluates every requested pattern; a deny fails immediately with DeniedError, an allow continues, and any 'ask' result inserts a pending entry, publishes Event.Asked and waits on the Deferred (registered so the entry is deleted on exit). reply('reject') fails the request and cascades a rejection to every other pending request of the same session; reply('always') records the request's always-patterns as approved rules and then auto-approves any other pending request of that session whose patterns are all allow under the new rule set.
invariants: A pending request must be removed from the map in all exit paths (ensuring) or the permission service leaks and blocks.
Rejecting one request must reject the other pending requests of the same session, so a user cannot be asked again for the same batch.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - on instance finalization every pending request is failed with RejectedError, so nothing is silently approved; a reject reply is a hard failure of the tool call.

name: session-permission-persistence
what: The session row stores a permission ruleset in a JSON column typed PermissionV1.Ruleset (permission/pattern/action). Session.setPermission writes it, and SessionPrompt.prompt derives allow/deny rules with pattern '*' from the request's per-tool overrides before storing them, so a later turn is evaluated against the stored ruleset merged with the agent's.
invariants: The stored session ruleset participates in every tool evaluation (merged with the agent ruleset), so writing it changes what the agent can do for the rest of the session.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - an unmatched request still evaluates to 'ask' even after a session ruleset is stored.

name: core-permission-service-v2
what: The v2 core permission service uses rules shaped {action, resource, effect} from the shared schema. A missing agent presents deny-all rules (const missingAgentPermissions, [{action:'*', resource:'*', effect:'deny'}]). evaluate() is the same last-match wildcard lookup defaulting to effect 'ask'; evaluateInput short-circuits to deny when any relevant rule denies, otherwise combines per-resource effects with deny > ask > allow; ask() only creates a pending request when the combined effect is 'ask', and assert() runs inside uninterruptibleMask so a permission decision cannot be abandoned mid-flight.
invariants: Effect combination across multiple resources must be deny > ask > allow.
The agent's own rules can never be widened by another ruleset: a deny in the relevant rules wins before any merge.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - a missing agent means deny-all; DeclinedError/CorrectedError/BlockedError are distinct failures and pending requests are declined on finalization.

name: no-os-level-sandbox
what: REFUTED that a sandbox exists: the only confinement is the permission model. Commands are built with ChildProcess.make and spawned through ChildProcessSpawner with no wrapper process, no namespace, no seatbelt/bwrap/landlock or seccomp layer; the only identifiers matching 'sandbox' in the tree are project git-worktree path bookkeeping (a project row column) and the codemode package's JS-level interpreter types. The model is told the same thing in prompt text: 'The operating environment is not in a sandbox'. A session's permission ruleset is policy, not confinement - an allowed shell command runs with the user's full OS privileges.
invariants: Because there is no OS confinement, a permission 'allow' is the ONLY gate between the model and the host; the permission layer must therefore never default to allow.
Anything relying on filesystem isolation (e.g. write-then-revert) must be implemented at the tool/permission level, not assumed from the OS.
failurePolicy: fail-open with respect to the OS - once a permission is allowed (statically or by the user) nothing prevents the process from touching arbitrary paths, so failures of the permission layer have host-level consequences.

name: mcp-and-external-directory-gates
what: Beyond the per-tool ask, two finer-grained gates exist. The shell tool asks for 'external_directory' with the scanned out-of-instance paths before asking for the shell itself. The MCP resource tools ask with permission 'read' and patterns of the form mcp:<server>:* (or the exact URI for a read), so an MCP server's resources are addressable by wildcard rules. Task delegation asks with permission 'task' and the subagent type as pattern.
invariants: MCP resources must be gated by the server-qualified pattern so one server can be allowed without allowing another.
Reading outside the instance directory must be a distinct permission from running a command.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - the ask is suspended until a reply; a deny fails the call before any read or spawn happens.
